name: SM_Seashell_Conch_PR

textures.channels: tangent normal, OpenGL (green up; flip green on import)
R occlusion, G roughness, B metallic

material_exception: unique BC/N/ORM bake private to this asset (not a row of ART_STANDARD.md section 2): the task for the unclaimed families asks for a baked set per asset, and the surface detail here (see dresses) does not exist in the shared library
pivot: base centre (bbox centre in X/Y, mesh bottom at z = 0), front on -Y
dresses: knobbed spiral sea shell (a conch or whelk), 14 cm, lying aperture-down: cream with two chestnut bands broken into flames, bleached spire, pink throat, sand in the hollows
status: source delivered; not imported into Unreal, not bound in families.json
known_weaknesses: One helico-spiral surface: the whorls pass through each other inside, the columella and inner lip are not modelled, and the aperture is a throat that narrows to a point rather than a spiral cavity. Knobs are a cosine of the spiral angle, so they are evenly spaced. The banding is procedural (two bands, axial flames); it is not a scan of a real species. 1,400 triangles on a 14 cm shell: the knobs are carried by the normal map more than by the silhouette. About a quarter of the texture holds the hidden inner whorl surfaces.
